design.summary: DESIGN R IS BUILT AS A WORKING SCRATCH PATCH AND MEASURED, NOT ONLY WRITTEN. Artifacts (all under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dadleet-src-skill-craft/f24838dd-d5f5-44a8-854e-3d9ddea18aed/scratchpad/b1012/r-design/): design-r-engine.patch (479 lines, 7 files, +344/-9: knowledge_home +292, navigator +32, workspace +14, progress_data +9, progress_render +1, counters +1, tests/shiploop_knowledge_support +3), design-r-packets.patch (61 lines, the fork-owned lines, applied separately), design-r-all.patch, design-r-tests/ (7 draft test files, 39 tests), mutate.py (23 mutants, all killed), survey.py/exp1.py/exp2.py/exp_route.py (real-data experiments), sw/ (patched copy), sw-base/ (pristine copy for fail-first runs). IMPORTANT FACTS FOUND ON THE WAY: (1) WT moved during my work from 8f3d4cbe to 6f86c8cf (fast-forward merge of origin/main = the E2E fork's release A, shiploop 0.59.0): knowledge_home.stage_files was replaced by required_earlier/next_close, STAGE_FILES gained prepare and release-verify, _stage_gates/_checked_line were reworded. All verification is on 6f86c8cf. Release A is merged, so the packet-text block no longer applies in the repository; I still give the packet lines as lines_for_fork and prototyped them (patch 2), but confirm no other fork branch is editing stage_lines before landing them. (2) The task text assumes a first run creates the living spec at handoff and the progress view should say 'created at handoff'. That belongs to the cut working-copy design: in the current YAGNI design the spec stage writes docs/shiploop/spec.md and the prepare close REQUIRES it (CLOSES['prepare']), so it exists from the spec stage on. No 'created at handoff' text is needed or built. (3) The plan says the planned record is the prepare close commit found by subject. Measured: that commit exists in 32 of 32 saved runs when searched by exact subject over the whole log, but a path-limited log (git log -- <feature dir>) finds it in only 8 of 33 folders because the prepare commit rarely touches the feature folder. So search by subject, never by path. (4) PRE-EXISTING RED at 6f86c8cf in a clean copy, not caused by this design: shiploop-e2e-commit-counters (test_the_leftovers_subject_and_the_two_announcements_are_in_shiploops_source: release A reworded the item commit announcement to 'ShipLoop committed W1's changes (its declared paths and documentation) as <sha>', so counters.ITEM_COMMITTED no longer matches it; the feat:<id> subject path still classifies), shiploop-status-display (2 failures), and shiploop-cross-run fails only without SHIPLOOP_PROGRESS=off SHIPLOOP_KEEPALIVE=off (a .progress.lock file). THE DESIGN IN SIX LINES: (a) knowledge.check(state,'handoff') gains the merge check, route-independent, at the gate before apply (fail-closed, nothing committed on a refusal); (b) the terminal _knowledge_close runs knowledge.commit, then knowledge.retire, then the existing follow-up return, so the removal commit travels with the return before the guard; (c) retire removes docs/shiploop/features/<f>/spec.md in its own commit only when the run's commits reach the user's branch (in-place or fast-forward), otherwise keeps it and says why; (d) FEATURE_LIST = docs/shiploop/features/README.md is rewritten from the tree inside knowledge commits only, and in the retire commit; (e) spec_pin/pin_notice give the plan a pin and a notice-not-refusal check; (f) the progress view shows a script-retired spec as 'merged'. No state key, no STATE_VERSION change, no new stage. Verified on the patched copy: every shiploop suite I ran passes except the pre-existing reds above (workspace 77, return-review 24, full-runtime 2, callback-contract, knowledge 49, lint, quality, test-loop, packets, dry-run, progress and about 40 more); a full-suite re-run was cut short for load after 20 of 68 suites, the packet-sensitive ones were run separately (see experiments).
design.retire_step:
WHERE. Two cooperating pieces, both fail-closed, no state key. (1) THE CHECK, at the gate: shiploop_knowledge_home.check(state, stage) gets a handoff branch. The early return 'if stage not in CLOSES and not _home_changed(repo)' becomes 'if stage not in CLOSES and stage != "handoff" and not _home_changed(repo)' so the check also runs when the home is clean, and the last line 'return ""' becomes 'return retire_refusal(state) if stage == "handoff" else ""' so every older refusal (missing files, credentials, dropped ID) is reported first. navigator._knowledge_gate already calls check for any done result on both the complete and improve-complete paths, before apply, so a refusal changes nothing (no commit, no state). (2) THE REMOVAL, at the terminal close: navigator._knowledge_close(terminal=True), after knowledge.commit and before the existing follow_up_knowledge_return: 'retired = knowledge.retire(after, _run_commits_reach_branch(after, root))'; a RuntimeError becomes NavigatorError('ShipLoop knowledge: ...; handoff remains pending.') exactly like knowledge.commit's. The follow-up return runs when 'committed.commit or retired.commit or terminal' (terminal was already enough). The order inside dispatch is unchanged and proven by tests: gate -> apply -> terminal close (commit pending home edits, retire, follow-up return) -> completion_guard -> save. Why not inside the gate alone: the route (return receipt) must exist and the removal must precede the guard so the follow-up return can carry it.
WHAT THE CHECK IS (knowledge_home._unmerged(repo, feature) -> Optional[List[str]]). Every requirement ID the feature spec mentions (existing regex _REQUIREMENT_ID = \b(R-\d+)\b over the whole file, any section) must be an ID of the living spec (the same regex over the whole living spec, so IDs under a Retired heading count). It is the SAME check for every format, with no format detection: of the 32 saved feature specs 2 use ## Added/## Modified/## Retired headings and 30 are stubs ('Adds: R-1 .. R-8. Modifies: none. Retires: none.' or 'Implements R-1..R-14'); none is a full copy. A range R-1..R-8 is read by its ends only (13 of 32 specs use a range, 114 IDs sit inside ranges; expanding them would have refused 0 of the 13, so expansion stays out as KISS, trigger to add it: a run ships a range whose middle IDs are missing). Returns None (cannot judge, so nothing is refused and nothing is removed) when the feature spec is not in the tree or when the living spec names NO requirement ID (the requirements may live in a team document: see project-knowledge 'Choose one authoritative home'). A feature spec with no IDs passes (nothing to merge). Measured: 0 refusals on all 32 saved feature specs against their living specs.
REFUSAL (exact, line 1 = fix + command; paths absolute): 'Before handoff is done, add R-9, R-12 to the living spec /abs/docs/shiploop/spec.md (or reword the mention in /abs/docs/shiploop/features/<f>/spec.md if it is not a requirement), then run the same complete command again.' then 'ShipLoop merges this run's feature spec into the living spec at handoff and then removes it, so every requirement ID the feature spec names must already be in the living spec; a retired one stays there under its Retired heading. Missing: R-9, R-12.' The verb is 'complete' because handoff has no Improve child (stage_spec handoff improve=None), matching the existing 'run the same complete command again' refusals. The wording claims only presence, not 'changed exactly as the feature spec says' (audit F24).
THE COMMIT. Its own commit, not folded into the terminal knowledge commit. Reasons: the body is script-built about the removal; progress_data and the harness identify it by subject (retired_by, counters); the deletion is one revertable unit; the pending-edit commit (a model fixing the living spec to satisfy the refusal) stays a plain knowledge commit made just before. Subject (knowledge_home.retire_subject(state)): 'docs(shiploop): merge <feature folder> spec into the living spec and retire the feature spec'. Staged through shiploop_git.commit_paths(repo, [<feature>/spec.md, FEATURE_LIST], message): add -A stages the deletion and the regenerated list, nothing else (verified: change set is exactly 'D spec.md' and 'M features/README.md'). Body, script-built (probe on a real repo, battleship-scoring clone):
  The run's requirement IDs are in docs/shiploop/spec.md; this commit removes the feature spec docs/shiploop/features/<f>/spec.md.
  Requirement IDs the feature spec named: R-1, R-2, ... R-10.   (or 'none.')
  Recover the removed file from this commit's parent: git show <this commit>^:docs/shiploop/features/<f>/spec.md
  <blank>
  Learned-from: <40-hex planned record> the feature spec as planned (prepare), the version this commit retires
  Learned-from: <40-hex last commit that changed the living spec> the living spec the feature spec's IDs were checked against
Citations use the existing grammar (shiploop_lessons.citations; both ids resolve through shiploop_git.resolve_commit, tested). NO lessons section: the script holds none (shiploop_lessons.lessons(message) == '' is asserted); the retire commit is a mechanical commit like leftovers and chain merges. PLANNED RECORD (knowledge_home._planned_record): 'git log -n 100 --format=%H%x00%s --fixed-strings --grep="record <folder> knowledge "' and the first (newest) row whose subject equals knowledge_subject(state, stage) for stage in (prepare, plan, test-strategy, spec). knowledge_subject is factored out of commit() so the subject is built in one place. Newest, because a replan can add later planning commits. Measured on the 32 saved runs: found at stage 'prepare' 32 of 32, and the feature spec at that commit equals the final feature spec in 32 of 32 (so it really is the historical record). When none is found (history rewritten, squashed, or the model committed the knowledge itself) the Learned-from line is simply omitted (tested: a history with no planning commit cites only the living spec); nothing is invented. The living-spec citation is the last commit touching docs/shiploop/spec.md.
IDEMPOTENCE / FAILURE. retire() returns Retired(commit, kept) (NamedTuple). It does nothing when reaches_branch is None, when the feature spec is not in the working tree (a retry, or a deletion by the model), or outside a work tree. It keeps the file (with a reason the navigator prints as 'ShipLoop knowledge: kept the feature spec <path>: <reason>.') when the route says no, when the merge cannot be judged, or when the file is not tracked and clean ('git cat-file -e HEAD:<path>' and 'git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path>'; this also protects a spec the credential screen left uncommitted). On a CommitError it puts the file bytes back and resets the index for the two paths, then raises RuntimeError, so a retry sees the file it started with (tested). A second call after success returns Retired('',''): the file is gone. Printed on success: 'ShipLoop knowledge: removed the feature spec <path> in <sha12> after checking that its requirement IDs are in the living spec; its last version is in that commit's parent.'
design.route_condition:
ROUTE CONDITION, one function: navigator._run_commits_reach_branch(after, root) -> Optional[bool]. It reads no state key and no run record: it reads the return receipt through a new read-only, lock-free helper shiploop_workspace.return_kind(workspace_root) -> Optional[str] (same shape as returned_before: _receipt(...), None on WorkspaceError or when status != 'returned', kind restricted to _RETURN_KINDS). A follow-up return keeps the first return's kind (_return_kind(prior_kind, ...)), so the answer does not change once recorded.
Table (names from ROUTE_TEXT/_RETURN_KINDS and execution_mode):
- execution_mode 'navigator' (in place, the user's own checkout): the run commits on the user's branch -> True -> remove. Tested end to end through the CLI (init, handoff, complete).
- 'navigator-worktree' + receipt kind 'fast-forward-merge': 'git merge --ff-only' puts the run branch, including the planning commits, on the user's branch -> True -> remove. The removal commit is then a knowledge commit made after the return; follow_up_knowledge_return returns it (see follow_up_return).
- 'navigator-worktree' + 'working-tree-return': kept files applied as a patch, 'no Git merge or commit' -> False -> KEEP the file (D3). It would otherwise be the only copy: I proved it (premise test) that a deletion committed in the worktree is carried as a patch, vanishes from the user's tree, and the user's branch history never contained the file.
- 'navigator-worktree' + 'no-change-return': nothing reached the source -> False -> keep.
- 'navigator-worktree' with no receipt yet: None -> retire is DEFERRED, no output. The same complete call then reaches the handoff guard, which refuses with the plan-return/review-return/return commands; after the return the retry runs retire with the route known. Tested (model calls complete before returning).
HOW THE HANDOFF STAGE LEARNS IT: from return-receipt.md at the moment of the terminal close; the handoff packet already prints 'Current workspace return: ... (kind: ...)' (so the model sees the same fact).
RETRY AFTER A REFUSED GUARD (audit F1/C1; handoff is retried in this order every time): attempt 1 retires and returns; if the guard then refuses (for example an uncommitted file the follow-up could not carry), the state is not saved but the retire commit exists. Attempt 2: the gate finds no feature spec -> passes; knowledge.commit has nothing; retire sees no file -> no second commit and no 'kept' notice; the follow-up return and the guard run again. Tested through the real CLI with a late uncommitted file: exactly one retire commit after both attempts, the second complete prints neither 'removed the feature spec' nor 'kept the feature spec'. Residual hazard, not mitigated: _check_submitted_evidence (now with an own_receipt parameter) refuses a retried handoff whose evidence_refs cite the removed file; 0 of 27 saved handoff results cite a feature spec, and the refusal already says 'Write the file or remove the reference'.
FIRST RUN: nothing special. The spec stage writes docs/shiploop/spec.md and the prepare close requires it, so the living spec exists and is committed by the 'after spec' knowledge commit; retire is the same as for any run. (The plan's 'created at handoff' is the cut working-copy design.)
NO REQUIREMENT CHANGES: the feature spec has no ID or names IDs already present; the check passes; the file is removed; the body says 'Requirement IDs the feature spec named: none.' where applicable.
FEATURE SPEC DELETED BY THE MODEL EARLY: no refusal and no retire. If uncommitted, knowledge.commit at the handoff close commits the deletion under the generic 'record ... knowledge after handoff' subject; retired_by() returns '' for it (subject differs), so the progress view keeps the true 'Document missing' warning. Its last version is in history (the spec stage and prepare commits). Tested.
NON-GIT CHECKOUT: exempt. check() already returns '' outside a work tree; retire() returns Retired('','') when 'git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree' fails. Tested.
LIVING SPEC FORBIDS COMPARISON (names no ID): keep, notice 'the living spec names no requirement ID, so the merge cannot be checked'. This also resolves audit F11 for repositories whose requirements live elsewhere.
design.follow_up_return: YES, the retire commit travels with follow_up_knowledge_return (P11) on the fast-forward route and in-place needs no return. Why: after the retire commit, 'git diff --name-only <receipt candidate head> HEAD' = [features/<f>/spec.md (deleted), features/README.md], every one passes knowledge_home.in_home (docs/shiploop/**), the worktree is clean, and plan_return auto-keeps docs/shiploop paths including a deleted, history-only file (the audit's 'checked and sound' item, now proven). execute_return then fast-forwards the source to the worktree HEAD ('prior_kind == fast-forward-merge' branch) and completed_receipt becomes current, so the guard passes. PROOF (draft tests, run against the real workspace module): shiploop-workspace test_the_retire_commit_is_returned_with_the_knowledge_follow_up_on_the_fast_forward_route: prepare a clean source, commit product + knowledge in the worktree, return (kind fast-forward-merge), commit the removal, follow_up_knowledge_return -> kind fast-forward-merge, source HEAD == worktree HEAD, the source no longer has the file, 'git show HEAD^:<path>' still returns it, completed_receipt(root, source) is not None. These premise tests pass before and after (the workspace code does not change); they pin the fact the design rests on. PATCH-APPLY ROUTE: no retire commit is made, so nothing needs to travel; the premise test test_on_the_working_tree_route_a_removal_would_be_a_patch_with_no_history_which_is_why_the_file_is_kept (dirty-start source -> working-tree-return; commit a removal in the worktree; follow_up_knowledge_return returns kind working-tree-return, source HEAD unchanged, the file disappears from the user's tree, 'git log HEAD -- <path>' is empty) documents why D3 keeps the file there. The end-to-end version of both routes through the real CLI is in shiploop-return-review (fast-forward: HEAD subject of the source is the retire subject and the file is gone; working-tree: file kept in worktree and source, notice 'kept the feature spec', no retire commit; in-place: retired in the user's checkout). New helper tested: workspace.return_kind (None before a return, 'fast-forward-merge', 'working-tree-return', unchanged across a follow-up, None for an unreadable workspace).
design.feature_list:
GENERATOR (knowledge_home): FEATURE_LIST = HOME + '/features/README.md' (not in CLOSES, STAGE_FILES, or KNOWLEDGE; a test asserts it is none of those). feature_list(repo) -> str: '' while docs/shiploop/features has no real (non-symlink) directory; otherwise the constant _LIST_HEADER followed by one row per folder sorted by name: '- [<folder>](<folder>/): [a.md](<folder>/a.md), [b.md](<folder>/b.md)' (only direct *.md files, sorted, symlinks skipped; a folder with no md file gets just the folder link). Derived from the tree only: no run state, no old file, no commit id, no timestamp, so the same text however often it is written. Each row is screened with privacy.sensitive_text; a flagged row is withheld and replaced by ONE trailing line '- N folder(s) not listed: the name looks like a credential. List them with `ls docs/shiploop/features/`.' (a folder name comes from the request's first six words). write_feature_list(repo) writes only when the text differs and is non-empty. It is called (1) inside knowledge_home.commit(), after the 'home changed' test and before commit_paths, and (2) inside retire() after the deletion, so it is in the retire commit; never in a commit of its own (tested: a stale list with a clean home is not rewritten and makes no commit; mutant 'write before the unchanged test' killed). A hand edit is replaced at the next knowledge commit. Before features/ has a folder nothing is written. earlier_features(state) returns the packet clause: 'Earlier features: none yet.' when no folder other than this run's own exists; '... <abs>/docs/shiploop/features/README.md lists every feature folder and the commands that find a requirement ID in them.' once the file exists; otherwise '... holds one folder per earlier run; ShipLoop writes their list, README.md, at its next knowledge commit.'
HEADER (exact, no requirement ID in it, because grep -rlw on an ID would otherwise list the list itself): '# Features' / 'ShipLoop writes this list from the folders beside it each time it commits knowledge; a hand edit is replaced. One folder is one run. At handoff ShipLoop checks that the requirement IDs a run's `spec.md` names are in the living spec ([../spec.md](../spec.md)), then removes that `spec.md`; the run's other files stay.' / 'Run these from the repository root (replace `<ID>` and `<folder>`):' / four bullets: (1) Features that mention a requirement: grep -rlw '<ID>' docs/shiploop/features/ (a range written R-n..R-m is found only by its two ends); (2) When a requirement was added, changed or retired: git log --format='%h %s' -G'(^|[^0-9A-Za-z])<ID>([^0-9]|$)' -- docs/shiploop/ ; (3) A removed spec.md, as last written: git show "$(git log --diff-filter=D --format=%H -1 -- docs/shiploop/features/<folder>/spec.md)^:docs/shiploop/features/<folder>/spec.md" ; (4) What a run planned: git log --format='%h %s' --fixed-strings --grep='<folder>' lists its knowledge commits; git show <commit>:docs/shiploop/features/<folder>/plan.md reads the plan as of one of them. Then '## Features' and the rows. No \b anywhere (audit F14).
COMMANDS TESTED LITERALLY on a probe (clone of the saved battleship-scoring repo after a real retire, macOS git 2.54, BSD grep and ugrep): grep -rlw 'R-9' lists test-spec.md, plan.md, system-tests.md of the retired run (not the removed spec); 'R-10' is not matched by 'R-1' (grep -w and the -G pattern both, checked on a fixture where a file holds only R-10); git log -G R-9 returns the retire commit among the commits that added or removed lines with R-9; the git show line prints the removed 'Feature spec: Battleship scoring' text; the planned lookup lists the run's 'record ... knowledge after spec / at prepare / ...' commits and the retire commit. The unit test test_the_headers_commands_work_on_a_retired_fixture runs them through sh -c. Not verifiable here: Linux git and GNU grep (OrbStack is stopped by the owner's standing decision, I did not start it); the same test runs on Linux CI, and the only non-trivial portability points are git log -G with POSIX ERE alternation and grep -w, both standard.
Real-data screens: feature_list was generated for all 31 saved knowledge homes and every line passed privacy.sensitive_text (0 flagged). Honest limit: after a retire, 'grep -rlw ID features/' finds a run only through its plan.md, test-spec.md, system-tests.md, release-plan.md or outcome.md, which models do write; a run whose only mention was its stub spec.md is found by the git log -G line instead.
Footprint: one extra row in a work item's change inventory and in the integrate packet's 'ShipLoop will commit' list when the list is modified inside the item loop (a new md file in the feature folder adds a link). Real inventories already list docs/shiploop/features/<f>/test-spec.md as 'A', so this is the same class; but the lint, quality and test-loop fixtures write all knowledge at prepare, after which the first list appears AFTER the item base and three tests failed (lint test_mode_off_runs_no_linter_but_records_the_change_inventory, quality test_packet_carries_script_authored_contract_rubric_and_inventory, test-loop test_the_integrate_packet_lists_what_shiploop_will_commit_and_what_it_leaves_with_one_sentence). Fix is in the fixture, not the engine: shiploop_knowledge_support.write ends with knowledge.write_feature_list(repo), standing in for the earlier knowledge commit a real run has (the list is created by the 'after spec' commit, long before any item base). Public name write_feature_list (not underscore) for that reason.
design.spec_pin:
FUNCTIONS (knowledge_home): spec_pin(state) -> Optional[str] = 'docs/shiploop/spec.md @ <12 hex>' of the NEWEST COMMIT THAT CHANGED THE LIVING SPEC ('git log -1 --format=%H -- docs/shiploop/spec.md'); None when that log is empty (no committed living spec) and None when the repo has no .git (a graph dry run runs no subprocess: shiploop-navigator-dry-run test_no_live_run_or_engine_calls caught my first version, which ran git there; guard added). Why not 'the commit the spec stage closed on': it needs a subject search or a stored value (no new state keys), and it is HEAD at that moment, which changes with every later commit; the newest-commit-touching-the-spec is stable under unrelated commits, so a plan written at plan time and a check made at the prepare close agree without remembering anything (tested), and it follows an Improve review or a test-strategy stage that edits the spec. A plan whose spec had uncommitted edits is pinned to the last committed version: accepted, all earlier closes commit before the plan stage.
CHECK (knowledge_home.pin_notice(state) -> str, '' when fine): first non-blank line of <feature>/plan.md must match ^Spec:[ \t]+docs/shiploop/spec\.md[ \t]+@[ \t]+<7-64 hex>. Three notices, each ending with the exact fix 'Make the first line of <abs plan.md>: Spec: docs/shiploop/spec.md @ <sha12>': (1) 'plan.md does not begin with the living spec's pin.' (2) 'plan.md pins a commit that <why from shiploop_git.resolve_commit>.' (3) 'plan.md pins the living spec at <sha12>, but the committed spec has changed since. Check that the plan covers the change.' Case (3) compares BLOB ids ('rev-parse <pinned>:docs/shiploop/spec.md' vs 'HEAD:...'), so a model that pinned HEAD (any commit with the same spec content) is accepted. A NOTICE, not a refusal (KISS and the critique's rule: gates that refuse need an observed failure; none exists; a refusal at the last planning stage costs a turn; the pin is a traceability aid). It is printed from navigator._knowledge_close when stages[-1] == 'prepare', after the commit, as 'ShipLoop knowledge: <notice>' on stdout, so the harness can count it from tool results and decide after one release whether a refusal is warranted. Rejected alternative, recorded: the script stamps the line itself at the prepare close (fully scripted, zero model compliance); not chosen because the line is meant as the model's claim of the spec version it planned against, and an edit of a model-owned file at a close is new behaviour; reconsider if the counted notices show the model rarely writes it.
PACKET TEXT FOR THE FORK (stage_lines, stage == 'plan', only when spec_pin(state) is not None; exact, two lines so the pin line is copyable): 'Begin plan.md with this exact first line, naming the living-spec version this plan implements; ShipLoop notes at the prepare close if it is missing or the spec has changed since:' then 'Spec: docs/shiploop/spec.md @ 3f2a9c1e0b7d' (value from spec_pin). Prototyped; passes packet-bounds, packet-completeness, guidance, dry-run and knowledge suites.
design.progress_view: CHANGE (shiploop_progress_data.build_snapshot, 9 lines, plus 1 line in shiploop_progress_render): inside the loop over candidate documents, before _read_document: 'if doc_id == "feature-spec" and not (base / relative).exists() and (retired := knowledge_home.retired_by(base, feature))' append a document {id, title, path, uri, content '', summary 'Merged into docs/shiploop/spec.md and removed by commit .', sha256 None, observed_at, status 'merged'} and a doc_identity row with status 'merged', and continue, so no 'Document missing: feature-spec.' warning is added. knowledge_home.retired_by(repo, feature) runs one read-only 'git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h%x00%s -- /spec.md' and returns the short id ONLY when that commit's subject equals the retire subject for this folder, so a spec the model deleted, or a folder never committed, stays 'missing' with its warning (true). Git is touched only when the file is absent. _DOC_STATUS_LABELS gets 'merged': 'Merged' (otherwise the raw 'merged' would render). The living-spec row is untouched: it is a real file from the spec stage on, so 'created at handoff' is not needed (see summary). Draft tests: shiploop-progress-data test_a_retired_feature_spec_shows_as_merged_with_its_commit_and_no_missing_warning (git repo fixture, retire-subject commit; asserts status merged, summary holds the short sha, no 'Document missing: feature-spec.' in warnings, other rows unchanged) and test_a_feature_spec_removed_by_any_other_commit_is_still_missing (passes before and after, a guard); shiploop-progress-render test_a_merged_document_renders_with_its_label_and_commit (page holds '>Merged' and the summary, not the raw lower-case status). Mutants killed: retired_by trusting any removal; the progress branch disabled; the label dropped.
design.dangling_links: Measured: 12 of 33 saved feature folders (32 with a spec.md) have docs/shiploop/README.md or SHIPLOOP.md text containing '<folder>/spec.md' (strict substring; reproduces the plan's '12 of 32'). After the retire those links dangle. The design does NOT rewrite model READMEs and does NOT gate on links (the plan's dropped 'handoff link gate' stays dropped: a README edit at handoff is another knowledge commit and re-stales the return). What it does: (1) packet text at the stages that write the README (plan and release-verify; exact line in lines_for_fork) says to link the generated features/README.md and not a feature's spec.md; (2) the generated list's header carries the recover command for a removed spec.md (command 3) and the retire commit body carries 'git show <this commit>^:<path>'; (3) no engine notice (a notice at the terminal close reaches nobody who can still commit); (4) measurable afterwards without engine code: a grep of README.md and SHIPLOOP.md for '<folder>/spec.md' on each finished run (optional harness knowledge_facts field, not built). Trigger to do more: a counted run where the packet line did not prevent the link and a person had to repair it.

design.spec_amendment: Its own commit, FIRST in the build order, subject 'docs(shiploop-e2e-spec): S-11 says the feature spec is the run's historical record, merged into the living spec and removed at handoff, and names the generated feature list', trailer 'No-Change-Note: harness spec amendment' (final paragraph with Co-Authored-By). Edits to test/shiploop_e2e/SPEC.md. (1) Replace the S-11 paragraph with: '**S-11 Knowledge is retained in the repository.** Planning knowledge (living spec, environment, test strategy, and per-feature plan, test and outcome records) is committed to the product's knowledge home, and the product itself ends committed on the source branch, so the next run builds on it instead of rediscovering it. A run's feature spec is its historical record once committed with the plan: at handoff ShipLoop checks that every requirement ID it names is in the living spec and, when the run's commits reach the user's branch (an in-place run or a fast-forward return), removes it in a commit of its own, so Git keeps every version; after a working-tree or no-change return no run commit reaches the branch, so the file stays. `docs/shiploop/features/README.md` lists the feature folders; ShipLoop writes it from the tree, only inside a knowledge commit.' (2) In the 'How the harness checks the clauses' table, S-11 row (the one ending '... replaces `shiploop.worktree_checks`'), append: 'A feature spec the run removed is not a missing file: `knowledge_facts` and the follow-on retention checks read the living spec and the files the prior repository tracks, never a feature spec.' (3) In the S-11/S-5 `commits` row, in the sentence listing the script class ('knowledge, empty baseline, leftovers, work-item and chain merge commits'), add 'the retire commit (docs(shiploop): merge <feature> spec into the living spec and retire the feature spec)'. Commit message body must state, per 'Evolving this spec': WHAT changed (S-11 text and two table rows); WHY (owner decisions D3 and D7 of 2026-10-10: the run's feature spec is a historical record that is merged and removed; a tree-derived feature list replaces model-written free text as the way to find an earlier feature); WHICH RUNS/BEHAVIOURS are affected: saved runs under /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs keep their feature specs (older engines) and are not regraded; a run on the new engine ends with no features/<f>/spec.md on the in-place and fast-forward routes (kept on the working-tree route) and gains docs/shiploop/features/README.md; metrics.commits.script gains one commit per such run (counters.KNOWLEDGE_SUBJECT widened in the later commit, classification before it counts the retire commit under 'other'); battleship-scoring retention check 1 compares only files the prior repository tracks and is unaffected; it supersedes the 09-26 S7 decision ('written once, kept as history') for spec.md only. Land it before any engine commit, as the SPEC requires.

The harness should count handoff refusals by first line in the first live pair (target 0). U2 THE CHECK IS PRESENCE ONLY: 'Modified R-2 (text...)' passes when R-2 exists even if the text was not merged; the removal is therefore limited to routes where Git keeps the file, and the retire body names the recover command. audits.verdict:
Buildable, with no hard blocker, and the core holds up. I rebuilt it on 6c555b59 (the engine patch minus one stale hunk, plus the packet patch). The designer's 39 draft tests pass; so do 14 further suites (e2e-commit-counters after rebasing the hunk, privacy, packet-bounds, packet-completeness, package-integrity, test-counts, store, local-skills, no-model-launch, generalized-discovery, repeatable-experiments, chain-async, chain-git, knowledge, navigator-dry-run, guidance). status-display has 1 failure, identical on pristine HEAD, and the design does not change it. shiploop-e2e and chain-lifecycle were still running under machine load when I stopped, so those two are unconfirmed.

Real-data results:
- The ID check refused 0 of 33 feature folders in 31 saved work repos (32 have a spec.md; the one model-named folder 'battleship' has none).
- The real retire, run on clones of all 32 specs, retired 32 of 32, each with exactly 'A features/README.md' and 'D <folder>/spec.md'.
- The planned record was found by subject at 'prepare' in 32 of 32 and equalled the final feature spec in 32 of 32.
- feature_list produced 0 flagged lines in 31 homes.
- The handoff widening risk measured 0: no credential-looking line in 325 saved knowledge .md files.
- The dangling-link count of 12 of 33 reproduces.

The refusals are the part that fails the KISS test:
1. The missing-ID refusal at the handoff gate has 0 observed failures behind it. The design used exactly that argument to make the pin a notice.
2. It is route-independent, so on a keep route it costs the run's last step and protects nothing.
3. It widens `check()` at handoff beyond what the retire needs.
4. The progress branch spawns Git inside a read-only observer on every snapshot from intake onward.
5. The pin check and one citation line add code with no consumer.

The safer alternative below removes all five while keeping D3 and D7.

If a result cites the feature spec and the guard then refuses, the retry is refused with 'evidence_refs cite files that do not exist ... Write the file or remove the reference'. 'Write the file' would recreate what the script just removed. The design counts 0 of 27 saved results citing it, but a one-line tolerance fixes it: treat a ref equal to the retired spec path, via retired_by or the retire subject, as present. 2. A kill between spec.unlink() and the commit leaves the deletion and the rewritten list uncommitted. Reproduced in test_12: the retry commits them under the generic 'record ... knowledge after handoff' subject, retired_by is '', and the progress view shows 'Document missing: feature-spec' (the same as the deleted-by-model case). It is safe, because the earlier gate already checked the IDs, but the recover-from-parent body is lost. Worth one sentence in U-risks. 3. The newest commit the next run's intake reads (recent_commits(3)) is now the 578-byte mechanical retire body with no lessons. In 31 of 31 saved homes the lessons-bearing release-verify commit is HEAD, so with one extra commit on top it stays inside the last 3. It still occupies a look-back slot with noise (the plan's own critique 5). Cheap fix: skip the retire subject in recent_commits, or shorten the body. 4. Claims I verified, so the main session need not repeat them: two consecutive follow-ups (a release-verify-style knowledge follow-up, then the retire) work and completed_receipt stays current (receipt nesting depth 2, 4.3 KB); replay of complete after done is a no-op; an index.lock failure restores the file and the next attempt succeeds with two commits (list, then retire); the reword exit works; a clean start whose review excludes a committed path falls to the working-tree route and the spec is kept. 5. The design's ID check relies on _KEY_VALUE_SECRET not matching list rows. I checked privacy.sensitive_text's patterns: \s*[:=] can span newlines, but generated rows start with '- [' and end in ')' or '.md)', so no row can trigger it. 6. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and skills/shiploop/README.md do not mention the feature spec (grep clean), so the doc list is complete as far as I could find.
audits.safer_alternative: Keep the design and change four things; none needs a new mechanism. (a) Restructure the terminal block of _knowledge_close into retire, then the follow-up, then print. On success print 'committed the removal of <abs path> in <sha12> and returned it'. When the follow-up returns None or raises after a retire commit, print 'committed in the run branch, not yet on your branch' and, on a raise, put the fix and command on line 1 as in correction 1. This makes every message true at the moment it is printed and keeps the retry story intact. (b) Say 'checks' and 'Retired', not 'merges' and 'Merged', in the refusal, the progress row and its label. Keep the task's commit subject. (c) Rebase the engine patch onto 6c555b59 (counters hunk only). Add the suite-catalog duration, or move the route tests to their own registered suite. Send lines_for_fork (1) to (6), with absolute paths and the stage-limited earlier_features, to the session that owns exp/step-slice-32c6ee. (d) Cut pin_notice and the three extra planned-record subjects, and the second Learned-from, to cut the code by about 70 lines. Measure the pin from the finished repo in the harness. A heavier but safer variant for users who squash-merge: record the removed spec's blob id in the retire commit body ('Removed spec blob: <sha1>') so that a later 'git show <blob>' works from any clone that still has the object, instead of relying on the commit parent. I did not test this and I would not make it a requirement.

audits.verdict: Sound and buildable, with corrections and no blocker. I applied the engine patch to a copy of WT HEAD 6c555b59, which is two commits past the 6f86c8cf the design verified on. All seven files apply except the counters.py hunk, whose context moved in bfceadc9. The packets patch also applies. On that copy, with a fixture-only retire-subject pin added to counters (the other design tests were not ported), I ran about 60 shiploop suites: knowledge, workspace, return-review (24 tests), full-runtime, callback-contract, progress*, lint, quality, test-loop, e2e, e2e-fidelity, run-review, cross-run, packet-bounds/-completeness, guidance, delegation and others. All pass. One suite, status-display, is red only at my long scratch path and is covered under correction 1. The designer's six scratch test files also pass on the patched copy: 39 tests, with the contract test needing the packets patch. I re-ran the shared sweeps: 0 of 32 feature specs refused by the merge check; the planned record found at "at prepare" in 32 of 32 and equal to the final spec in 32 of 32; 12 of 33 README/SHIPLOOP.md files link the folder's spec.md; 0 of 31 saved handoff results cite a feature spec. All 31 saved receipts are fast-forward-merge, so the retire runs in practice. All 27 returned worktrees end clean, so the follow-up return has nothing to refuse on. Symbols, signatures and call order are as claimed: gate before apply, then terminal close (commit, retire, follow-up), then guard, then save. Two things in the task text are only partly honoured: the "merge" is a presence check of requirement IDs, and the retire commit carries a second citation that is not needed. Both are under corrections and cuts below.

corrections.claim: retired_by 'touches git only when the file is absent' (progress_view).
corrections.evidence: The file is absent for the whole pre-spec window of every run. The observer calls build_snapshot every 2 s under a shared lock, and the CLI's run_lock uses a blocking flock(LOCK_EX). Each tick would run `git log --diff-filter=D -- path`. It costs 18 ms here (with commit-graph) but is unbounded on large histories.
corrections.fix: Call retired_by only when the run is at handoff or done, since the script retires only at the terminal close. Also retitle the row ('Feature specification (merged)'); it keeps 'draft' today.

audits.safer_alternative: Keep the design and ship C0 to C4 as one minor with these changes. (a) Stage FEATURE_LIST in the retire commit only if it is tracked or not ignored; otherwise commit the deletion alone. (b) Rename the commit to say 'check ... and retire', and keep the removal sentence out of the header until the retire exists. (c) Gate the progress lookup on handoff or done. (d) Have write_feature_list overwrite only a file it generated, never a symlink. (e) Derive the counters pattern from knowledge_home. (f) Re-measure the suite durations and add the LEARNINGS entry. Defer C5, the pin notice, until a counter exists; keep spec_pin for the plan packet line. Land the packet lines (C6) last, as planned. If the owner wants a stronger route test than the receipt kind, git can answer it directly: `merge-base --is-ancestor` of the planned-record commit against the source branch tip. That needs the manifest's source repo and branch and adds no state, but I would keep the receipt reader: it works, it is tested end to end on both routes, and the kind is already written there.
